Sign / phenotype feature: New or progressive persistent proteinuria
Evidence class: ASH guideline + direct comparative EHR cohort
Typical timing vs diagnosis: Can precede diagnosis; often becomes the renal trigger
Population / context: Adult with otherwise unexplained proteinuria, especially with monoclonal/plasma-cell context
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: proteinuria 17% AL vs 6% ATTRwt. ASH 2026 recommends paraprotein testing for unexplained proteinuria.
Why it matters for suspicion: One of the most useful ordinary-care transitions from vague illness to possible AL organ involvement.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: AA and non-amyloid kidney disease also cause proteinuria; diabetes/HTN may coexist.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: New/progressive proteinuria + MGUS/SMM/MM or another unexplained organ system
Threshold / criterion status: ?0.5 g/24 h, predominantly albumin, is a consensus AL renal-involvement criterion—not a validated universal pre-test screening cutoff.
Recommended use in phenotype model: Core trigger; prioritize persistence and trend.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Nephrotic-range proteinuria / nephrotic syndrome
Typical timing vs diagnosis: Usually near diagnosis; often later than low-grade proteinuria
Population / context: Adult with unexplained heavy proteinuria ± edema/hypoalbuminemia
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: nephrotic syndrome 6% AL vs <1% ATTRwt.
Why it matters for suspicion: Highly discriminating for AL versus ATTR once a protein-losing renal phenotype is present.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: AA and primary glomerular disease remain major alternatives.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Nephrotic proteinuria + monoclonal/plasma-cell context
Threshold / criterion status: Use standard nephrotic definitions (~3–3.5 g/day depending source); threshold is not AL-specific.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Multisystem accumulation across ?3 organ-system domains
Quantitative / comparative evidence: In 1,523 adults, ?3 systems were involved before/at diagnosis in 54%; median first-sign-to-diagnosis interval 2.7 years.
Why it matters for suspicion: Cross-specialty accumulation is more informative than isolated nonspecific symptoms.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: ATTRv is also multisystem; ATTRwt is more cardiac/orthopedic dominant.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Protein-losing renal phenotype + cardiac and/or neurologic/GI/systemic signs
Threshold / criterion status: ?3 systems is descriptive, not a hard screening gate.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Monoclonal/plasma-cell precursor state PLUS new unexplained organ dysfunction
Population / context: MGUS/SMM/MM patient who develops new renal, cardiac, neurologic, GI, hepatic or soft-tissue abnormality
Quantitative / comparative evidence: AL clonal diagnoses and renal/GI/neurologic precursors are enriched before AL diagnosis compared with ATTRwt.
Why it matters for suspicion: Combination is more informative than MGUS or an organ abnormality alone.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Incidental MGUS is common in ATTR; subtype remains unresolved until appropriate work-up.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Clone + new proteinuria/nephrotic syndrome, cardiac injury, neuropathy or multisystem change
Threshold / criterion status: No validated single composite threshold; literature-backed EHR synthesis feature.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Macroglossia / acquired tongue enlargement
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Macroglossia is a classic soft-tissue manifestation much more associated with AL than ATTR.
Why it matters for suspicion: When genuine and unexplained, it is a strong subtype clue.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Rare; not exclusive to AL; other causes exist.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Macroglossia + purpura, proteinuria, clone or cardiac disease
Threshold / criterion status: Clinical finding; no numeric threshold. Tongue biopsy is not a screening requirement.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Periorbital / pinch purpura or spontaneous unexplained ecchymosis
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Classic AL-oriented sign but uncommon.
Why it matters for suspicion: High subtype value because it is not a typical ATTR prodrome.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Anticoagulation, thrombocytopenia, senile/steroid purpura and trauma mimic.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Purpura + macroglossia, nephrotic phenotype or plasma-cell context
Threshold / criterion status: No validated numeric threshold.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Known plasma-cell dyscrasia / smoldering myeloma / multiple myeloma
Typical timing vs diagnosis: Can precede organ manifestations by years
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: multiple myeloma history 29% AL vs 2% ATTRwt.
Why it matters for suspicion: A known clone materially raises AL prior probability when new organ dysfunction emerges.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Most plasma-cell disorders do not cause AL; ATTR may coexist with monoclonal gammopathy.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Plasma-cell disorder + new renal/cardiac/neurologic/GI/hepatic abnormality
Threshold / criterion status: Tufts ?-MGUS/SMM dFLC >23 mg/L + IGVL/cytogenetic enrichment is study-specific, not a universal criterion.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: multiple myeloma; SMM; plasma cell dyscrasia
Recommended use in phenotype model: Strong background-risk feature; combine with organ signal.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Pre-existing abnormal monoclonal studies from MGUS/myeloma follow-up + new organ signal
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Typed AL cohort: combining serum/urine IFE and sFLC captured monoclonal abnormalities in nearly all AL patients.
Why it matters for suspicion: A pre-existing clonal lab signal plus new organ dysfunction substantially strengthens AL suspicion.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: CKD can distort FLC ratios; ATTR may coexist with monoclonal gammopathy.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Prior monoclonal abnormality + new proteinuria/HF/neuropathy/GI/systemic change
Threshold / criterion status: Once AL is suspected, ASH recommends SIFE+UIFE+sFLC. Use age/eGFR/assay-aware FLC ranges (e.g., 0.48–3.38 at eGFR 30–44; 0.54–3.30 at eGFR <30 in iStopMM).
Recommended use in phenotype model: Use as pre-test context only if testing existed independently of amyloid suspicion.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Hypoalbuminemia with edema / anasarca
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Low albumin and edema frequently accompany nephrotic renal AL.
Why it matters for suspicion: With proteinuria they define a stronger renal cluster than edema alone.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: HF, cirrhosis, malnutrition, protein-losing enteropathy and AA nephrosis mimic.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Proteinuria + falling albumin + edema
Threshold / criterion status: Albumin <3.5 g/dL is common clinical hypoalbuminemia, not an AL-specific cutoff.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) under surveillance
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: monoclonal gammopathy 22% AL vs 9% ATTRwt; separate ATTR cohorts reported MGUS in 39% ATTRwt and 49% V122I ATTR.
Why it matters for suspicion: MGUS raises AL suspicion only when compatible new organ changes appear.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Incidental MGUS is common in ATTR and with aging.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: MGUS + new proteinuria/nephrotic syndrome or multisystem disease
Threshold / criterion status: If SIFE/UIFE/sFLC are ordered because amyloid is suspected, they are second-stage tests; pre-existing surveillance results may be used as prior context.
Likely EHR location: Problem list; hematology notes; prior labs
Recommended use in phenotype model: High-value context with explicit ATTR guardrail.
Ranking interpretation: AL-supportive feature ranked using suspicion strength, subtype discrimination, evidence quality, pre-test usability, EHR detectability, and actionability.

Sign / phenotype feature: Disproportionate NT-proBNP/BNP or troponin elevation
Typical timing vs diagnosis: May precede overt HF, especially in monitored clone populations
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Consensus cardiac involvement includes NT-proBNP >332 ng/L in absence of renal failure/AF; biomarkers are central to AL cardiac assessment.
Why it matters for suspicion: Can reveal occult cardiac injury, but does not type amyloid.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Renal dysfunction, AF, ACS and ATTR-CM also elevate biomarkers.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Biomarker rise + monoclonal context or renal/multisystem AL pattern
Threshold / criterion status: >332 ng/L is an organ-involvement criterion with exclusions; Mayo staging cutoffs are prognostic, not pre-test diagnostic thresholds.
Recommended use in phenotype model: Moderate support, strongest in clonal-risk patients.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Renal dysfunction / falling eGFR with proteinuria or monoclonal context
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: CKD 43% AL vs 37% ATTRwt; renal signs common in prodrome.
Why it matters for suspicion: Renal decline gains value with proteinuria and clonal context.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: CKD alone is common and poorly discriminating.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: eGFR decline + proteinuria + clone or another unexplained system
Threshold / criterion status: Use eGFR-aware FLC ranges in CKD; standard 0.26–1.65 should not be universally applied.
Recommended use in phenotype model: Moderate feature; low weight if isolated CKD.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Symmetric peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy / sensory loss
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: other polyneuropathies 21% AL vs 17% ATTRwt; neurologic involvement common in AL prodrome.
Why it matters for suspicion: Adds a second/third organ system and may be early.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: ATTRv, diabetes, toxins and paraproteinemic neuropathies overlap.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Neuropathy + proteinuria/clonal history; absence of strong hereditary/autonomic phenotype
Threshold / criterion status: No EMG or sural-biopsy sensitivity should be used as a pre-test threshold; nerve biopsy is not screening.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: sensorimotor polyneuropathy; sensory loss; axonal neuropathy
Recommended use in phenotype model: Moderate AL feature; compare ATTRv actively.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Persistent diarrhea / constipation / dysphagia
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: dysphagia 18% AL vs 10% ATTRwt; constipation 27% vs 18%; diarrhea 19% vs 11%.
Why it matters for suspicion: Collectively more common before AL than ATTRwt.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: ATTRv has prominent GI/autonomic disease; common GI disorders remain common.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: GI symptoms + proteinuria/clonal context or multisystem accumulation
Threshold / criterion status: No AL-specific threshold.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Early satiety / nausea-vomiting / unexplained abdominal pain
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: nausea/vomiting 20% AL vs 12% ATTRwt; abdominal pain also more common in AL.
Why it matters for suspicion: Strengthens multisystem AL and helps distinguish from cardiac-dominant ATTRwt.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: ATTRv and common GI disease overlap.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: GI symptoms + renal/clonal evidence, weight loss or neuropathy
Threshold / criterion status: No validated symptom-frequency cutoff; gastric-emptying studies are not required for pre-test screening.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: early satiety; nausea; vomiting; abdominal pain
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Unexplained hepatomegaly and/or cholestatic ALP elevation
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Consensus criteria: liver span >15 cm without HF or ALP >1.5×ULN after amyloid established elsewhere.
Why it matters for suspicion: Adds another system to a systemic AL pattern.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Congestive hepatopathy is a major confounder; liver disease, malignancy and AA overlap.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Hepatic abnormality + renal/clonal/cardiac evidence
Threshold / criterion status: >15 cm and >1.5×ULN are organ-involvement criteria, not validated standalone screening cutoffs; specificity of low ALP threshold has been questioned.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Unintentional weight loss / declining weight
Typical timing vs diagnosis: Can occur >1 year before diagnosis in some cohorts
Population / context: Unexplained weight loss with GI/autonomic or multisystem disease
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: weight loss 12% AL vs 8% ATTRwt.
Why it matters for suspicion: Useful as longitudinal systemic clue when paired with organ signs.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Malignancy, infection, ATTRv and many GI disorders overlap.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Weight loss + proteinuria, early satiety, neuropathy or clonal history
Threshold / criterion status: Do not impose >10% loss as a universal AL threshold.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Unexplained heart failure / HFpEF
Population / context: Unexplained HF, especially with LV thickening
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: HF 45% AL vs 72% ATTRwt.
Why it matters for suspicion: Strong reason to consider cardiac amyloidosis, but poor AL discriminator.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: ATTRwt is more commonly preceded by HF; hypertension/valve disease are common mimics.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: HF + nephrotic/clonal evidence supports AL; HF + CTS/AF/spinal stenosis favors ATTRwt
Threshold / criterion status: Wall thickness >12 mm is an organ-involvement criterion when no other cause exists, not a universal HFpEF screening definition.
Recommended use in phenotype model: High amyloid score, intentionally low AL subtype weight.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Unexplained increased LV wall thickness / restrictive physiology on routine echocardiogram
Quantitative / comparative evidence: AL and ATTR both produce infiltrative wall-thickening patterns; ATTR often has greater wall thickness.
Why it matters for suspicion: Routine echo can convert nonspecific HF symptoms into infiltrative-cardiomyopathy suspicion.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: ATTRwt/ATTRv overlap; hypertension, AS and HCM mimic.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Echo red flag + renal/clonal AL context; orthopedic prodrome favors ATTRwt
Threshold / criterion status: >12 mm is a classic involvement criterion, not a sensitive universal screening threshold.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: wall thickness; restrictive filling; valve/septal thickening
Recommended use in phenotype model: Enter amyloidosis pathway; do not type AL.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: ECG low voltage / voltage-to-mass discordance / pseudoinfarction
Population / context: Thick-wall phenotype with unexpectedly low QRS voltage
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Classic cardiac amyloidosis clue.
Why it matters for suspicion: Supports infiltrative cardiomyopathy but not AL subtype.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: AL and ATTR overlap; low voltage has incomplete sensitivity.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Low voltage + wall thickening + AL-oriented renal/clonal features
Threshold / criterion status: No single ECG criterion is sufficient for AL.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: low QRS voltage; pseudoinfarction; voltage-mass discordance
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Unexplained cardiomyopathy / cardiomegaly without AL-oriented extracardiac features
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: cardiomyopathy 24% AL vs 48% ATTRwt; cardiomegaly 30% vs 46%.
Why it matters for suspicion: Raises amyloidosis suspicion but comparative frequency actually leans ATTRwt.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Hypertension/HCM/ischemia/valvular disease and ATTR are major alternatives.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Cardiomyopathy + proteinuria/clonal context makes AL more plausible
Threshold / criterion status: No subtype-specific threshold.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Autonomic dysfunction / orthostatic hypotension
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Autonomic/hypotension diagnoses occur before AL diagnosis, but are not AL-specific.
Why it matters for suspicion: Can signal systemic amyloid neuropathy.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: ATTRv often has earlier/more prominent painful small-fiber and autonomic/GI disease; medications/diabetes mimic.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Autonomic dysfunction + proteinuria/clonal context supports AL; family/ocular/painful PN favors ATTRv
Threshold / criterion status: Routine orthostatic BP is pre-test usable; formal amyloid-directed autonomic testing is later-stage.
Recommended use in phenotype model: Amyloidosis red flag, low AL subtype weight.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Hypotension / syncope / dizziness in a multisystem phenotype
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: hypotension 25% AL vs 18% ATTRwt; syncope 19% vs 14%; dizziness 28% vs 24%.
Why it matters for suspicion: Adds autonomic/cardiac systemic evidence.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Very nonspecific; drugs, dehydration and arrhythmia mimic.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Hypotension/syncope + proteinuria/clonal context or neuropathy
Threshold / criterion status: No AL-specific numeric cutoff beyond routine definitions.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Pleural effusion or recurrent unexplained serosal fluid
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: pleural effusion ~20% in both AL and ATTRwt with no meaningful subtype separation.
Why it matters for suspicion: Can support systemic/cardiac illness, but adds almost no AL-vs-ATTR information.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: HF, malignancy, infection, renal/liver disease common.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Effusion + proteinuria/clonal/multisystem AL phenotype
Threshold / criterion status: No AL-specific threshold.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Dyspnea / shortness of breath
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Large prodrome cohort: dyspnea 59%; matched EHR: 48% AL vs 58% ATTRwt.
Why it matters for suspicion: Can be early but is not AL-oriented.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: ATTRwt, lung disease, anemia and other HF etiologies overlap.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Dyspnea + renal/clonal evidence raises AL; CTS/AF/older cardiac pattern leans ATTRwt
Threshold / criterion status: No threshold.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Fatigue / malaise / weakness
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Large prodrome cohort: fatigue/malaise 61%; matched EHR: 40% AL vs 30% ATTRwt.
Why it matters for suspicion: Frequent early symptom but low specificity.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Nearly every chronic systemic illness can cause it.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Useful only when organ-specific signs accumulate
Threshold / criterion status: No threshold.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Edema without documented proteinuria or hypoalbuminemia
Quantitative / comparative evidence: Matched EHR: edema 34% AL vs 32% ATTRwt—essentially nondiscriminatory.
Why it matters for suspicion: Edema alone adds very little.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: HF, venous disease, liver disease, medications and ATTR overlap.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Becomes meaningful with proteinuria + hypoalbuminemia
Threshold / criterion status: No threshold.
Recommended use in phenotype model: Very low weight unless renal cluster present.
Ranking interpretation: Contextual/general amyloidosis evidence; useful mainly when combined with AL-oriented features.

Sign / phenotype feature: Credible chronic inflammatory/autoinflammatory/infectious history + new persistent proteinuria
Population / context: RA, Crohn, FMF, chronic infection or another strong AA driver
Quantitative / comparative evidence: AA guidelines center suspicion on chronic inflammatory states followed by renal manifestations.
Why it matters for suspicion: Strongly redirects a renal amyloid phenotype toward AA when the inflammatory driver is credible.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: AL and inflammation can coexist; clonal evidence may keep AL active.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Persistent inflammatory driver + inflammatory burden + new proteinuria
Threshold / criterion status: No universal CRP/SAA or duration threshold establishes AA.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: RA; Crohn; FMF; TB; bronchiectasis; proteinuria
Ranking interpretation: Clinically important guardrail/counter-evidence; intentionally down-weighted as an AL-positive signal.

Sign / phenotype feature: Older patient with predominantly isolated cardiac phenotype + AF/CTS and little renal/GI/clonal evidence
Quantitative / comparative evidence: ATTRwt had markedly more HF, cardiomyopathy, AF and CTS; AL had more renal/GI/clonal diagnoses.
Why it matters for suspicion: Practical guardrail against converting 'possible cardiac amyloid' into 'possible AL'.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: AL can present cardiac-only; not a hard exclusion.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: HF/cardiomyopathy + AF + CTS/spinal stenosis without strong AL-oriented extracardiac context
Threshold / criterion status: Composite synthesis, not validated exclusion rule.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: HF; AF; CTS; spinal stenosis; no heavy proteinuria
Recommended use in phenotype model: AL down-weight; route toward ATTR evaluation.
Ranking interpretation: Clinically important guardrail/counter-evidence; intentionally down-weighted as an AL-positive signal.

Sign / phenotype feature: Painful length-dependent/small-fiber neuropathy with early marked autonomic/GI dysfunction ± hereditary clues
Quantitative / comparative evidence: ATTRv literature emphasizes painful small-fiber neuropathy with autonomic/GI red flags; AL can also cause neuropathy but lacks the same hereditary pattern.
Why it matters for suspicion: Prevents generic amyloid neuropathy from being counted as AL-positive.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: AL neuropathy, diabetes and CIDP overlap.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Painful PN + orthostasis/GI dysfunction + family/ocular/cardiac hereditary clues
Threshold / criterion status: No single feature proves ATTRv; genetic testing is confirmatory.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: small fiber neuropathy; burning pain; dysautonomia
Ranking interpretation: Clinically important guardrail/counter-evidence; intentionally down-weighted as an AL-positive signal.

Sign / phenotype feature: Bilateral/recurrent carpal tunnel syndrome years before cardiac disease
Typical timing vs diagnosis: Often 5–9 years before ATTR cardiac diagnosis
Quantitative / comparative evidence: CTS is enriched in ATTR but comparable to general population in AL; matched EHR: 28% ATTRwt vs 12% AL.
Why it matters for suspicion: A long CTS prodrome should push toward ATTR rather than AL.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: CTS is common and can coexist with AL; not an exclusion.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: Bilateral/recurrent CTS + later HF/LVH/AF/conduction disease
Threshold / criterion status: Timing matters more than a single CTS code.
Ranking interpretation: Clinically important guardrail/counter-evidence; intentionally down-weighted as an AL-positive signal.

Sign / phenotype feature: Long orthopedic prodrome: lumbar spinal stenosis / distal biceps rupture / multiple tendon-hand procedures
Quantitative / comparative evidence: ATTR literature links orthopedic-to-cardiac trajectory to ATTRwt; lumbar stenosis was also higher in ATTRwt than AL in matched EHR.
Why it matters for suspicion: Prevents an ATTR phenotype from being mislabeled AL.
Key overlap / mimic / guardrail: Age-related degenerative disease can mimic individual events.
Combination that strengthens interpretat: ?2 orthopedic red flags + later HF/LVH/AF/conduction disease
Threshold / criterion status: No validated orthopedic score; use clustering and timing.
Example structured fields / NLP terms: lumbar stenosis; biceps rupture; trigger finger; tendon surgery
Ranking interpretation: Clinically important guardrail/counter-evidence; intentionally down-weighted as an AL-positive signal.
